title.full: What to do after a scam

summary.text: Act immediately: alert your bank, secure Singpass if needed, lock CPF withdrawals if eligible, and report to police.

steps.name: Alert your bank
steps.text: Alert your bank to freeze the affected bank account immediately.

items: Alert your bank to freeze the affected bank account immediately.

steps.name: Reset your Singpass password
steps.text: If you think your Singpass has been compromised, reset your password.

items: If you think your Singpass has been compromised, reset your password.

about.text: For further assistance, contact the official Singpass helpdesk at 6335 3533.

steps.name: Activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock
steps.text: If you are 55 and above, activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock under Account settings to disable online CPF withdrawals instantly.

items: If you are 55 and above, activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock under Account settings.
This disables online CPF withdrawals instantly.

steps.name: File a police report
steps.text: File a police report and provide all details.

quotes.text: In the unfortunate event that you fall prey to a scam, we recommend taking the following actions immediately:
Alert your bank to freeze the affected bank account.
Reset your Singpass password if you think your Singpass has been compromised.
If you are 55 and above, activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock under Account settings to disable online CPF withdrawals instantly.
File a police report and provide all details.
For further assistance, please contact the official Singpass helpdesk at 6335 3533.
